scope: Published general reference facts for apparently healthy adults, including published pregnancy and lactation categories at ages19–50. Exploring a category never establishes a personal life stage or assesses intake.

nutrientNotes.vitamin_c_mg: Smoking adds 35 mg/day to the Vitamin C requirement in the source; no smoking adjustment is calculated here. This does not raise the UL.
nutrientNotes.magnesium_mg: The magnesium UL covers pharmacological agents only and excludes food and water.
nutrientNotes.calcium_mg: Health Canada uses the 2011 calcium reference values, which supersede 1997 values. Equal adjacent age bands are coalesced only when sex, reference type, amount and intake scope all agree.
nutrientNotes.potassium_mg: Health Canada uses the 2019 potassium values. These are Adequate Intakes (AI), not EARs or RDAs. Intake below an AI does not establish inadequacy. No potassium UL or CDRR is established in this source; that does not mean unlimited intake is safe. These general references are not a treatment target.
nutrientNotes.vitamin_d_ug: Health Canada uses the 2011 vitamin D values, assuming minimal sun exposure. These are dietary amounts in micrograms per day, not blood vitamin D measurements or a treatment dose. No IU, blood-level or D2/D3-form conversion is calculated here. The UL covers total intake and is not an intake goal.
nutrientNotes.vitamin_a_ug: Vitamin A requirements are expressed as retinol activity equivalents (RAE). The upper limit applies to preformed vitamin A only, not all carotenoids. A total RAE food value or a label with unknown form does not establish the preformed amount. No retinol/carotenoid/IU conversion or comparison to your intake is calculated here.
nutrientNotes.folate_ug: Folate requirements use dietary folate equivalents (DFE). The upper limit uses micrograms of folic acid from supplements and fortified foods, not DFE or naturally occurring food folate. Existing total-folate food fields and labels with unknown form do not establish DFE or the synthetic amount. No conversion, pregnancy/preconception dose or intake assessment is calculated here.
nutrientNotes.vitamin_e_mg: Vitamin E requirements refer to alpha-tocopherol in 2R-stereoisomeric forms. The upper limit applies only to synthetic vitamin E from supplements and fortified foods. A source field without stereoisomer or formulation details does not establish either basis. No IU/activity conversion or intake assessment is calculated here.
nutrientNotes.iron_mg: The source female iron requirements assume menstruation before age 51 and post-menopause from age 51. Profile sex and birth year do not establish either status for an individual. The source also reports higher requirements for vegetarian diets; no personal adjustment is calculated. These reference facts do not estimate absorption or individual inadequacy probability, particularly with menstrual losses. The UL is not a treatment dose.
nutrientNotes.vitamin_b12_ug: Vitamin B12 has no established UL in this source; that does not mean unlimited intake is safe. Dietary amounts do not establish absorption or blood B12 status. The source notes that food-bound B12 absorption can be reduced in older adults and discusses fortified foods or supplements for those over 50. This is general source context, not an inferred personal absorption problem or a supplemental dose recommendation.
nutrientNotes.vitamin_k_ug: The source publishes vitamin K Adequate Intakes (AI), with no established UL; that does not mean unlimited intake is safe. Intake below an AI does not establish inadequacy. The available generic food field reports phylloquinone, not all vitamin K forms. No conversion or personal clotting/medication assessment is calculated.
nutrientNotes.sodium_mg: Health Canada uses the 2019 sodium values. AI and CDRR have different meanings: CDRR is the intake level above which reduction is expected to reduce chronic disease risk in an apparently healthy population. It is not a UL, a normal interval or a personal treatment target. No sodium UL is established in this source. These facts do not set or change your saved meal-planning targets.
nutrientNotes.zinc_mg: The source reports higher zinc requirements for vegetarian diets, especially diets based mainly on grains and legumes. These published base requirements assume the source mixed-diet context; saved preferences or incomplete logs do not establish an actual dietary pattern. No personal adjustment, absorbed amount or compound-to-elemental conversion is calculated.
